newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: De Beers to raise Botswana market cap.
newsitem.headline: De Beers to raise Botswana market cap.

text.p: South African diamond giant De Beers' planned listing on the Botswana stock exchange should increase the market capitalisation of the bourse at least 50 fold, a spokesman said on Thursday.
"We got the first prize early," Botswana Stock Exchange chief executive and acting chairman Alan Norrie told Reuters.
"It is a clear demonstration of what can happen on the investment front when a country liberalises its exchange control policy," he said.
De Beers announced on Wednesday it would list its De Beers/Centenary linked units on the stock exchanges of Namibia and Botswana on March 6 and 7 respectively.
De Beers has its primary listing in Johannesburg, while De Beers Centenary is listed in Switzerland.
Norrie said De Beers would list 380.2 million shares at Thursday's price of 156.50 rand.
The current market capitalisation of the exchange is 1,200 million pula and -- once listed -- De Beers will account for 97 percent of the aggregate total of the exchange.

"This is what we hoped for in November last year when the Bank of Botswana announced the liberalisation of exchange controls," Norrie said, adding that financial players were pleasantly surprised at the speed of the liberalisation.
